pr_title: resolved: demote only the fallback servers in the global scope
pr_body:
This softens the behavior introduced in c83cd8da4916, and simultaneously expands the role of fallback servers so they are applied not only when there are no dns servers configured, but when all the configured dns servers are configured only for non-default-route links.

The intent is that the global FallbackDNS (instead of DNS) can now be used in conjunction with the per-link dns, providing a fallback behavior without introducing a scope overlap.

~~Fixes: c83cd8da4916 (resolved: demote the global unicast scope)~~ (Reverted)

---

Closes: #33835 (again)
Replaces: #34047

Regardless, it might be nice to include an extra section on there to explain how this fallback logic works in more detail (I don't understand the logic enough to send a PR myself unfortunately)

@Winterhuman that content looks accurate to me. I don't think this change has any bearing on VPNs.

This fallback is only needed when we don't have any other suitable DNS servers to use — the user did not specify a desired server, the network did not inform us of a local dns via dhcp or any other protocol, the query name does not match the search or route domains of any link, and any vpn/other interfaces present that do have DNS configured are excluded from general use by the default-route=no flag.

issue_context.title: Use fallback dns servers for default route links
issue_context.body:
### Component

systemd-resolved

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe

If I intend to use only the DHCP provided DNS servers, I can make a network file like so:

```
[Match]
Type=ether

[Network]
DNSDefaultRoute=yes
DHCP=yes
```

But, if I then connect to a network where the DHCP server does not inform us of any DNS servers, no DNS servers are configured and all queries are rejected with

```
$ resolvectl query example.com
example.com: resolve call failed: No appropriate name servers or networks for name found
```

### Describe the solution you'd like

sd-resolved should probably use the configured fallback servers in this case, or possibly a per-link fallback setting? There should be some kind of fallback behavior in case the local network configuration doesn't provide DNS.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

Manually configure a dns when one isn't provided by the local network.

### The systemd version you checked that didn't have the feature you are asking for

256.4

enp7s0 is default-route, no global DNS server is configured. The wireguard iface has 2 route-only domains configured.

             93.184.215.14                     -- link: enp7s0

$ resolvectl status
Global
           Protocols: -LLMNR +mDNS -DNSOverTLS DNSSEC=yes/supported
    resolv.conf mode: stub
  Current DNS Server: 8.8.8.8#dns.google
Fallback DNS Servers: 8.8.8.8#dns.google 8.8.4.4#dns.google

The global scope and fallback dns server is considered only if there is no dns configured on any link.

When enp7s0 is default route, I'd like some fallback behavior if the there is no DHCP provided dns server, even if I have the wireguard iface present.
